mame.instructions:
A live MAME debug session.

TOOLS. Session: `start`, `rom_check`, `focus`. Advance: `run_to`, `run_for`, `step`, `resume`, `trace`. Read: `read_memory`, `read_block`, `registers`, `disassemble`, `find`, `history`, `palette`, `screen_view`, `gfx_view`, `gfx_locate`, `gfx_sweep`, `gfx_draft`, `gfx_blits`, `gfx_blit_source`. Write: `write`, `set_register`, `reset`. Scan: `scan_start`, `scan_filter`. Comments: `comment_add`, `comment_delete`, `comment_load`. Lua: `input`, `record`, `audio_record`, `state_save`, `state_load`, `screen_signature`, `lua`. Console: `debug`.

A SESSION. `start` parks the machine STOPPED. `run_to`, `run_for` and `step` stop it again, with a survey; `run_to`'s target has no stop of its own. `resume` lets it RUN. While it runs the readers refuse (`not_stopped`); these answer: `breakpoint_at`, `breakpoint_clear`, `breakpoint_list`, `captures`, `comment_list`, `comment_save`, `cpu_info`, `gfx_film`, `gfx_load`, `log`, `log_wait`, `machine_map`, `palette_log`, `regpoint_add`, `regpoint_clear`, `regpoint_list`, `scan_clear`, `snapshot`, `state_list`, `status`, `stop`, `symbols_find`, `throttle`, `watch_add`, `watch_clear`, `watch_list`, `registers(from_last_stop=True)`, `perform`, `drive`, `close`. A stop reached on its own is `stopped_on_its_own`. `rom_check` reads 16 bytes at `reference_addr` against `reference_rom` at `reference_base`. A wait that ran out is `verdict: TIMEOUT`, `ok`. `memdump` and `snapshot` answer with a PATH.

CPUS: no `cpu` acts on the VISIBLE one (stops move it), lists or clears all; named, moves only `step`'s.

ADDRESSES are written `0x`, a condition as typed; any other ref is a symbol, bare hex naming none refused. Breakpoints are at PLACES, never expressions.

EVERY REPLY carries `summary`, `status` (`ok`, or `INVALID` with `code` and `message`) and `session` (`altered` after a write). A wrong TYPE is the schema's `bad_argument`. `not_settled`: `stop`, and if `stop` fails as well, `close` then `start`. `session_broken` LATCHES until `close`.

Reference: REFERENCE.md.

tools.name: read_memory
tools.description:
Read `length` bytes of memory at `ref` (a symbol name or a `0x` address), `length` in
1..1024, of `cpu` (`subcpu`; the visible one when empty). Each cpu is served by its own thread of the gdbstub's thread patch (`status`'s `threads`); a build without it serves its first cpu alone, whatever is visible, and refuses another (`bad_argument`). A range whose last byte lies past that cpu's program space (the address mask `start` read) is `bad_argument` naming the mask; with no mask known the range is the console's.

Reply: `addr`, `length`, `hex`, `cpu` (the one read). Above the ceiling the answer
is `memdump`, which writes to a file: a read comes back as hex text, two characters per byte,
and a frame of VRAM through it is a haystack in the conversation rather than data. A range whose
read side is unmapped (a write-only block, `latch` to `symbols_find`) answers ZEROS here with no
error: the values live in the share behind its handler, and `read_block(ref=...)` reads them.
Needs the machine STOPPED: on a running one the reply is `status: INVALID` (`not_stopped`) with `last_stop` and `answers_while_running`.

Reference: REFERENCE.md, Reading and writing.

tools.name: watch_add
tools.description:
Declare a WATCH at `ref`, in its cpu's byte order. STORED, re-armed at the next `start`.

Arguments:
- `mode`: `show` (read at each stop, arms nothing), `change` (a WRITE watchpoint: a write
  stops the machine, and `watch_hit` says WHO WROTE THIS BYTE), `count` (tallies
  every write by value and writer pc, never stopping), `capture` (one
  row per access to `trigger`, never stops) or `expr`
  (`ref` is ONE reading debugger expression, `beamy`: no `,`, `;`, assignment, length or
  fmt).
- `ref`: a symbol, a `0x` address, or a place through a POINTER (`[base]+0x28`,
  `base->field`), re-resolved each stop; a capture's `ref` is what each row HOLDS.
- `fmt`: a scalar (`u8` .. `f64`), an array (`u16[8]`), a string
  (`char[16]`) or a struct (`{x:i16,y:i16}`). `auto`: a typed symbol's type, else the WIDEST
  unsigned scalar `length` divides.
- `length`: TOTAL bytes, REQUIRED unless `fmt` is sized or the symbol is typed; at most
  128 for a show or capture watch, 1024 otherwise.
- `by`: `auto` unless forced.
- `cpu`: its cpu, else the visible one.
- `condition` (change only): stop only on a write it holds for (`breakpoint_at`'s grammar
  on the row's cpu; `wpdata` is the value written).
- `trigger`, `trigger_type` (capture only): the symbol or `0x` address whose WRITES (`w`)
  or READS (`r`: of `ref` itself; no length, fmt or block) make rows.
- `space`: `io` when `ref` (count) or `trigger` (capture) is a `0x` PORT; session-only.

Refused: a change watch on an unmapped write; a count range splitting a bus word;
a ref declared again another way; a range another declaration arms; what the console
cannot evaluate; an unknown pointer base or `cpu`.
Works on a RUNNING machine, not through a POINTER (`not_stopped`).

Reply: `ref`, `by`, `mode`, `stored`, `already_stored`, `armed`, `state`, `while_running`; at a
place `length`, `fmt`, `addr` once resolved, `pointer` through one, `reading` when stopped; and
each mode's own fields (REFERENCE.md, Declarations; rows: `watch_list`).

Reference: REFERENCE.md, Declarations.

tools.name: memdump
tools.description:
Write `length` bytes of memory from `ref` of `cpu` (`subcpu`; the visible one when empty) to
the file `dest`, and CHECK the file.

Reply: `addr`, `length`, `path`, `bytes`, `cpu` (the one dumped). The dump is written by MAME's
own console `save`, so the bytes never cross the socket; the file must then be exactly `length`
bytes and its first bytes must equal a protocol read of the same range (the known-answer
control), else the reply is `status: INVALID` with `message`; a control read that breaks the
channel is `session_broken` naming the `path` the file was left at. `dest` must be absolute, in a directory that exists, with no comma, semicolon, quote, whitespace, bracket or control character,
and not there yet. A range whose last byte lies past that cpu's program space (the address mask `start` read) is `bad_argument` naming the mask; with no mask known the range is the console's. A range that wraps would hang the console's
`save`, and one past the space never reaches it. The control reads the same cpu, through its own
thread of the gdbstub's thread patch; a build without it reads only its first cpu, and another
is refused. Each refusal happens before `save`, so a refused call never leaves a file behind. A
control read the stub refuses is `readback_refused`; one that breaks the channel is
`session_broken`, which LATCHES. Needs the machine STOPPED: on a running one the reply is `status: INVALID` (`not_stopped`) with `last_stop` and `answers_while_running`.

Reference: REFERENCE.md, Reading and writing.

tools.name: status
tools.description:
Whether a machine is alive, and which one. Safe on a running machine; a stop it finds
the machine reached on its own is recorded and reported in `stopped_on_its_own`.

Reply: `alive`; with no machine, a `note` when the server closed the last session after an hour
with no call; with `exit_code` and a `note` when MAME died under the session (`close` collects
its last words before anything is deleted); when alive also `system`, `pid`, `stub_port`,
`scratch_dir`, `state_dir`, `cfg`, `debugger` (`attached`, and a `note`: a capture taken at a
stop here can land a frame away from an autoboot golden), `fingerprint` (the build the
declarations are judged against, the first cpu's) and `fingerprints` (each cpu's),
`errorlog_path`, `stdout_path`, `running`, `pc` (the machine's, read now; absent while it runs
or once the session broke: `last_stop.pc`), `last_stop` (`stop_seq`, `pc`, `cpu`, `frame`,
`how`, `since_s`, `wall_at`; the park after `start` is stop 1), `in_debugger` (`breakpoints`,
`watches` (the change watches) and `regpoints`: each `ref` this server armed in the debugger,
and its `cpu`), `threads` (the stub's thread per cpu; empty without the thread patch), `cpus`
(what each is doing is `cpu_info`'s), `frame_symbol` (the frame counter's name as `start` asked
it, unavailable on a board with none), and, always present, `console_pending` (Lua lines sent
and not yet evaluated, which `close` drains before its `quit`), `throttles_pending` (`mark`,
`on`) and `tallies_pending_removal` (`tally_id`, `call`), where a switch that landed is its row
leaving. `broken` (absent on a healthy session) says why it can no longer be trusted: the
machine is then asked nothing, `running` reads false, and the way out is `close`, then `start`.

Reference: REFERENCE.md, The session.

dosbox-x.instructions:
A live DOS machine in DOSBox-X.

TOOLS. Session: `build_check`, `start`, `status`, `close`. Read: `registers`,
`read_memory`, `disassemble`, `call_stack`, `memdump`, `find`, `log`, `log_wait`,
`machine_map`, `interrupt_vectors`, `palette`, `screen_view`, `screen_signature`,
`debug`. Scan (by value, with no map): `scan_start`, `scan_filter`, `scan_clear`.
Write: `set_register`, `write`. Advance: `run_to`, `run_for`, `trace`, `screen_wait`,
`step`, `resume`, `stop`. Declarations, kept per conf: `breakpoint_at`,
`breakpoint_list`, `breakpoint_clear`, `breakpoint_interrupt`, `watch_add`,
`watch_list`, `watch_clear`. States: `state_save`, `state_load` (by menu, windowed),
`state_list`. Names: `symbols_load`, `symbols_find`. Comments: `comment_add`,
`comment_list`, `comment_delete`, `comment_save`, `comment_load`. Input: `send_keys`,
`send_mouse`, `drive`. Captures: `captures`, `capture_frame`, `snapshot` (by menu,
windowed). Sequences: `perform`.

A SESSION. `build_check` answers about the BUILD, never a reading, and REFUSES while a
session is live. `start` parks the guest STOPPED at the debugger; `resume` lets it
run. The readers need it STOPPED and refuse otherwise, naming `last_stop` and what
answers; a running guest is reached through `log`, `log_wait`, `send_keys` and
`send_mouse`, and stops at a breakpoint armed BEFORE the release
(`breakpoint_interrupt` 0x21 real mode, 0x31 ah=2 DJGPP) or, WINDOWED only, at `stop`;
a headless `resume` with no stopper needs `until_close=True`. What you declare while
it runs is `pending` until the next stop. After `symbols_load`, a `ref` is a symbol or
a `SEG:OFF`. A sequence is ONE call: `perform`, or `drive` for an input and its check.
FOR A VALUE use `registers`, `read_memory`, `memdump` or `log`; `debug` is the last
resort.

EVERY REPLY carries `summary`, `status` (`ok`, or `INVALID` with `code` and `message`)
and `session` (`altered`: has anything here written to the machine?). An argument of
the wrong TYPE is the schema's `bad_argument`.

Reference: REFERENCE.md.

tools.name: step
tools.description:
`count` instructions, one at a time, `mode` `into` (F11, the default) or
`over` (F10), each step READ BACK. Needs the machine stopped.

Reply: `before` and `after` (address and CPU mode), `completed` (how many steps actually
landed, not how many were asked), `running` (the machine left the debugger, e.g. an
`over` across a call that never returns, so the remaining steps were not sent), `moved`,
`stalled` (steps that did not change position: a swallowed keystroke), and the stop's
`instruction`, `registers`, `watches`, `attribution` and `e9`, the log summary as in `resume`:
`e9` is `none` (default), `all` (the whole log), `lines:N` (the last N), `since` (every line
since the previous stop) or `seconds:N` (needs `e9_stamp`), filtered by `e9_filter`. About a
second and a half per
step; for a longer run use `run_to`.
